summary: Any three distinct array values contain a middle value that has a smaller and a larger witness in the complete array, so a correct answer requires only fixed work and no input-length scaling.

optimality.argument: Producing the required integer decision requires Omega(1) work. For n at least three, inspecting any three distinct values and returning their median takes O(1) work; for smaller n, returning -1 also takes O(1).

replacement_checks.evidence: Every correct implementation must inspect enough input state to produce one integer result, requiring at least constant work.
The reference reads only the length and first three distinct values, then uses a fixed number of arithmetic and comparison operations.
Authored cases cover lengths one and two, exactly three values, additional values after the inspected triplet, unsorted values, and both value boundaries.
